APPROVED ON SEPTEMBER 2, 2026

# REGULAR MEETING OF THE SOUTH BURLINGTON SCHOOL BOARD

Wednesday, August 12, 2026
Executive Session at 5:00 pm
Regular Session at 6:00 pm
South Burlington School District Administrative Office
577 Dorset Street, South Burlington, VT

## REGULAR MEETING

Seamus Abshere, Dan Boyer, Emilee Hoffman, Michelle Boyer, Elissa Galvez, Tom Chittenden

**ADMINISTRATION/STAFF**
Dr. Joe Clark

None

Seamus Abshere, called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.

## EXECUTIVE SESSION

The Board convened in Executive Session at 5:30 p.m.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to enter executive session at 5:30 pm to discuss employment of a public officer or employee, labor negotiations, and receiving confidential attorney-client communication for the purpose of providing legal services to the Board as permitted under Vermont law and added that it would be significantly disadvantageous to the district not to do so in executive session.

## REGULAR MEETING

**Present**
Seamus Abshere, Dan Boyer, Emilee Hoffman, Michelle Boyer, Elissa Galvez, Tom Chittenden, Momin Waqar, Oliver Kunz

**Administration/Staff**
Dr. Joe Clark, Matt Currier, Deirdre Phalon, Suzanne Gruendling, Nicole Carter, Daisy Brayton, Jean-Marie Clark, Nick Bocchino

None

Chair Seamus Abshere called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm. The Pledge of Allegiance was said.

## ANNOUNCEMENTS AND AMENDMENTS TO THE AGENDA

**Announcement**
Seamus Abshere said the board did talk about labor negotiations in executive session.

**Amendments to the Agenda**
Michelle Boyer asked if the revisions of Executive Limitation 2.4 should be tabled as this is really the work of the school board. She suggested discussing this but not moving forward with a first reading this evening.

Seamus Abshere presented four proposed amendments:

- Move items in #6 discussion items before the start of the community forum.
- Move the 2026-2027 Academic Calendar and the first three action items under agenda item #7 before the community forum.
- Remove first reading from item #6 Executive Limitations Policy 2.4.

Dan Boyer moves to approve the agenda as amended Emilee Hoffman seconds. No discussion. All in favor and the motion passes.

**Comments and Questions**
No public comments were received.

## Focus on Student Learning

There was no student.

## DISCUSSION ITEMS

### Revised Executive Limitation 2.4 Financial Condition and Activities

Dr. Joe Clark stated that the district has lots of employees throughout the school district that are signing contracts, and it's been his experience, and that of the business office, that signing contracts is typically reserved for the superintendent or his or his or her designee.

Dr. Clark said one of the important changes would be to detail policy #10 that the board would, annually, at its organizational meeting, make a motion that the superintendent or designee is the one who has the authority to enter into contracts. So, all contracts, except those he designates to a few folks, would be signed by the superintendent.

Dr. Clark said the other changes in the policy are recommendations from the business office so that the policy is more in line with our current practice. The board reviewed Executive Limitations Policy 2.4 and it will be brought back to the next meeting as a first reading after review by the Chair Abshere.

### 2026-2027 Academic Calendar (Holidays)

Dr. Clark said when the district adopted the recommended calendar from the Champlain Valley Superintendents Association it did not include several of the holidays that had been included the prior year and the district received great feedback from our families that celebrate Diwali. They indicated that November 11th was not really when South Burlington families celebrated the Diwali holiday. The 11th is really a different holiday that is only celebrated by a few of our families so they suggested changing the date to November 10th. He added the he knows this is disruptive to the district school schedules, but he thinks that if we are going to honor our families, we should honor the day that they would celebrate.

The board agreed to change the celebration of Diwali on the 2026-2027 Approved Academic Calendar from November 11th to November 10th.

## ACTION ITEMS

### Designate Authorized Contract Signatories and Delegate Contracting Authority Pursuant to 16 V.S.A. § 563(16)

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to Designate Dr. Joe Clark and his designees as Contracting Authorities Pursuant to 16 V.S.A. § 563(16).

Michelle Boyer moves, Emilee Hoffman seconds. No discussion. All in favor and motion passes.

### Designating board member to serve on Act 170 merger committee

Seamus Abshere said there were two committees formed relating to the Act 170 merger committee. This board needs to designate a school board member to serve on the CESA committee. This committee would be where the area school boards would come together with other school districts and make a good faith effort to consolidate. The committee member is required to be a school board member. Seamus Abshere said he would be willing to serve on the Act 170 merger committee on behalf the board. The board discussed the timeline of the committee work.

Emilee Hoffman moves, Dan Boyer seconds. No discussion. All in favor and the motion passes.

### Approve VSBA Superintendent Evaluation contract

The board discussed using the Vermont School Boards Association for the Superintendent Evaluation process at a cost of $2,500.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to authorize the chair to sign the VSBA Superintendent's Evaluation contract for the coming school year. Dan Boyer moves and Michelle Boyer seconds. No discussion. All in favor and motion passes.

## COMMUNITY FORUM ITEMS

### Discuss First Draft of the Ends Policy Update

The board introduced the agenda item, explaining that the presentation represented the culmination of several months of community engagement conducted to assist the Board in revising the District's Ends Policy.

Michelle Boyer said the Ends Policy Committee prepared a preliminary report of the 2026 Ends Policy Review and Revision. The full report is available on the school district website.

Michelle Boyer gave the background about what an actual Ends Policy is for South Burlington. Michelle said it is a statement that describes student outcomes valued by the South Burlington community and their reason for being.

- The board is responsible for establishing the Ends consistent with the Community's values.
- The District is responsible for the Means to achieve the Ends.

Michelle Boyer provided an overview of the process used to develop a new Ends Policy for the district.

Seamus Abshere and Michelle Boyer reviewed the specific details of the current Ends Policy versus the suggested new Ends Policy.

There was a lengthy discussion about the revised policy. The board will have a first reading of the revised Ends Policy at the August 19 meeting.

### Collect Initial Questions about NESDEC Best Use Study

Board members did not receive any questions regarding the NESDEC Best Use Study.

## ACTION ITEMS (Continued)

### Monitoring Report 2.2 - Treatment of Staff

Daisy Brayton discussed the details of Monitoring Report 2.2 - Treatment of Staff. She reviewed the overall gaps including:

- Employee handbook is extremely outdated and needs revision (last revised in 2014).
- Policy and procedure interpretation and implementation have been inconsistent.
- Annual support staff performance evaluation process has not been managed and very few evaluations are being done.
- Complaints, concerns, and resolutions were not being tracked or documented consistently.
- Employees panorama data has not been shared or evaluated.

Daisy Brayton review the path to improvement, including:

- Continue to improve the clarity, accessibility, and consistency of employee-related policies, procedures, and operational practices by finalizing the Employee Handbook and Financial Operations Handbook.
- Evaluate and improve the Employee Annual Review process to include reviewing and updating the current process, train employees on the process, and monitor compliance with the process.
- Strengthen employee engagement, trust, and overall organizational culture by acquiring feedback and survey data to identify opportunities for improvement.
- Develop and implement a strategic plan to increase employee awareness of available resources, supports, and reporting pathways.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to review the rubric for Monitoring Report 2.2 - Treatment of Staff. Dan Boyer moves and Michelle seconds. No discussion. All in favor and motion passes.

The board reviewed the Monitoring Report Rubric.

### Monitoring Report 2.1 - Treatment of Students and Parents/Guardians

Dr. Joe Clark reviewed Monitoring Report 2.1 including:

Big Gap Overall:

- Response and resolution times are not measured districtwide.
- Complaints, concerns, resolutions, and corrective actions are not centrally tracked.
- The District does not consistently document whether communications are understood or how student and family input influences decisions.
- Privacy, accessibility, and security-video implementation data are incomplete.
- Evidence is not yet consistently collected across schools and departments.

Path to Improvement:

- Monitor belonging goals in every school and District Continuous Improvement Plan.
- Establish clearer expectations for acknowledging, responding to, and resolving concerns.
- Implement consistent complaint and concern tracking.
- Review communications and forms for clarity, accessibility, and minimum-necessary information collection.
- Strengthen documentation of student and family input.
- Track privacy, accessibility, and security-video implementation more consistently.
- Use common annual evidence submissions from schools and departments.
- Implement the Director of Equity, Belonging and Family Engagement role and the new Welcome Center.

Momin Waqar discussed the student perceptions at the high school.

Seamus Abshere called for a motion to review the rubric for Monitoring Report 2.1 Treatment of Students and Parents/Guardians. Dan Boyer moves and Emilee Hoffman seconds. No discussion. All in favor and motion passes.

The board reviewed the Monitoring Report Rubric.

## SUPERINTENDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Joe Clark reviewed the work that has been happening across the district this summer. He said there is a significant amount of work happening across all of the buildings including facilities work, technology work, and professional learning and planning.
